summary: Recover interrupted pre-backend agent starts without retaining blocked workspace admission

replay.detail: Retained objective evidence and replay behavior are unchanged.

schema.detail: No SQLite schema, index or store-version changes. Existing runtime operation JSON carries an additive backend-entry fence.

rules.detail: Dispatch records an owner- and operation-bound before-backend fence in the same write. A durable backend-entering advance is required before invoking either runtime backend. Recovery under the start lock revokes and closes an abandoned before-backend operation through the existing completion witness writer, releasing admission for a replacement.

compatibility.detail: No claim fields or client interfaces change. Earlier readers ignore the additive operation JSON field. Missing, legacy, mismatched and backend-entering fences retain conservative interrupted-worker recovery.

downtime.detail: No additional downtime beyond the normal daemon upgrade.

manual.detail: No user action is required. Previously stranded legacy operations do not gain a new non-launch proof.

recovery.detail: A restart during capture or timeout backoff can retain a before-backend closure witness. A crash after the backend-entering fence remains conservative, even if no backend was actually started. A failed fence advance prevents launch and completes with before-backend proof. Rolling back ignores the new JSON field without a data migration.
